tr: Good morning. I'd like to open a business checking account. I just started a small landscaping company.
Congratulations. I'll need your business license and a photo ID. Do you have those with you?
I've got my ID, but I didn't know I needed the license. It's at my office.
That's all right. We can start the application now, and you can upload a copy of the license from home through our Web site.
That would be great. And is there a monthly fee?
It's free for the first year. After that, it's ten dollars a month.
Hello, I bought this jacket here last week, but the zipper broke the first time I wore it. I'd like to exchange it.
I'm sorry about that. Let me see if we have another in your size. Hmm, it looks like we're out of mediums here, but our Oak Street store has two.
I'm on my way to work, so I can't go there today.
I can have one sent to your home at no charge. It should get there by Thursday. Do you have your receipt?
Thanks for volunteering at the university's open house this Saturday. Kenji, you'll be at the welcome table. Mark, you'll lead the campus tours.
Sure. How many visitors are you expecting?
About four hundred. That's more than last year, so we've added a second tour at two o'clock.
Do you have a map of the new science building? I haven't been inside it yet.
I'll e-mail one to you tonight. Could you both come at eight-thirty? The doors open at nine.
I'll be there, but I may be a few minutes late. My bus doesn't get in until eight-thirty-five.
Hi, I'm thinking of getting a family membership to the museum. What are the benefits?
It's ninety dollars a year. It covers two adults and up to three children, and you'd get free entry to all our special exhibits.
That sounds reasonable. Is there free parking as well?
Not at this location, but members get half off at the garage next door. And if you join today, you'll receive a free tote bag.
OK, I'll sign up. We're here to see the dinosaur exhibit. Is it on this floor?
It's on the second floor. Just take the stairs behind you.
Thanks for calling Summit Auto Service. How can I help you?
Hi, I brought in my van this morning for an oil change. I just got a text message saying it needs new tires as well. How much would that cost?
Let me see. For your model, it's about four hundred and eighty dollars for all four.
That's more than I wanted to spend. Are the tires really that bad?
The two front ones are worn, but the back ones are still fine. You could replace just those two for two hundred and forty dollars.
Let's do that. Can I still pick the van up at four?
You should be able to. We'll call you if anything changes.
Marco, the editor needs your article on the Riverside housing project by noon. How's it coming along?
I've finished the writing, but I'm still waiting on one quote from the city planner.
We go to print at two.
I know. I've left her two messages already. If I don't hear back by eleven, I could use what she said at last week's council meeting.
That should work, as long as you check it against the recording. And send me the photos, too. I'll need to choose one for the front page.
Rosa, do you drive past Hill Road on your way to work? My car's at the repair shop until Wednesday.
I do. I could pick you up at seven-thirty if that's not too early.
That'd be perfect. I usually start at eight anyway. Let me pay for your gas.
There's no need. But could you do something for me? I've got to leave at three on Tuesday for a doctor's appointment. Would you be able to cover the front desk for an hour?
Hi, I'd like to send this package to Vancouver. How long will it take?
Standard post takes five to seven days, and it's twenty-two dollars. Express takes two days, and that's forty-five dollars.
Oh, it's a birthday present, and her birthday's on Friday. I'd better go with express.
All right. I'll need you to fill out this customs form, since it's going to Canada. Please list what's inside and how much it's worth.
Sure. Do you have a pen?
So, we've interviewed three people for the sales manager job. What did you two think?
I liked Ms. Duarte. She's run a team of twenty, and she knows the medical equipment market.
She's got great experience, but she'd need to move here from Lima, and she'd want help with that.
We've paid moving costs before, haven't we?
Yes, for the head of engineering. It was around five thousand dollars.
In that case, I'm happy with her. Should I call her with an offer?
Let me talk to the president first. I'll let you know by tomorrow morning.
Hello, Mr. Sharma? It's Claire from Sweet Layers Bakery. I'm calling about the wedding cake you ordered for June sixth.
You asked for fresh strawberries on top, but our supplier says that they won't have any that week because of the recent storms.
Oh, my fiancée really loves strawberries.
I understand. We could use raspberries instead. Or, I could decorate the cake with strawberries made of sugar. They look just like the real thing.
Hmm, I'd have to ask her. Can I call you back this evening?
Of course. We're open until seven.
Hi, Amy. I just looked at the hotel's rates for our sales workshop in May. We've got about thirty-five people attending.
Right, but don't forget that the Singapore team might come. That'd be ten more people.
Oh, I didn't realize that. Then we'd better take the next size up, to be safe.
Agreed. And can you ask if lunch is included? Last year, the food cost us more than the room did.
I'll call them this afternoon. I also need to find out if they have a projector.

tr: Hello, Mrs. Chua. This is Adam from Lakeshore Kitchens. We've finished the cabinets, and we're ready to install them on Monday as planned. But I just found out that the granite for your countertops won't be here until Thursday. So we can do the cabinets on Monday, then come back on Friday for the countertops. You won't be able to use the sink until then, I'm afraid. If that's a problem, we could do everything at once next week. Just let me know which you'd prefer. You can reach me on my cell phone until six.

Attention, passengers. The 9:15 express train to Glasgow will now depart from platform four, not platform seven as shown on your ticket. We apologize for the change, which is due to a track inspection. Passengers should allow at least ten minutes to reach platform four, since the east escalator is out of service. If you need assistance, please speak to a member of staff at the information desk. Refreshments will not be available on this train today, but there's a coffee cart at the entrance to platform four.

Good morning, and welcome to the Hartley Art Museum. My name's Sofia. On this tour, we'll be looking at works by American painters of the 1920s. We'll start in Gallery C, which has just been reopened after being closed for a year. Please remember that you shouldn't touch the paintings, and that bags larger than a laptop must be left at the coat check. The tour lasts one hour. Afterward, I recommend that you see our new exhibit of photographs on the third floor. It's free today only. Now, if you'll follow me.

Let's look at the third-quarter numbers. Overall sales are up eight percent, which is excellent. Most of that came from our new line of running shoes. But returns have also gone up. Customers say that the shoes run small. So, the design team is working on a new size chart for the Web site. Now, I know that some of you think that we should just change the product. Well, the factory has already produced fifty thousand pairs. Let's see if the size chart helps first. I'll report back at next month's meeting.

Good evening. City officials have approved the budget for a new public library in the Westfield neighborhood. Construction is expected to begin next spring and to take about eighteen months. The library will include a children's reading room and a community meeting space. Mayor Alan Brooks says the project will cost twelve million dollars, and that most of it will come from a recent bond measure. Residents are invited to see the architect's plans at City Hall this Saturday. In sports news, the Westfield Hawks won their third game in a row last night.

Hi, Dr. Palmer. This is Jill Lambert from the Northern Business Forum. We'd love to have you as our keynote speaker at this year's conference on November fifth. I read your book on team leadership, and I think that our members would learn a lot from you. We usually give speakers a fee of two thousand dollars, and we also cover travel. I realize that you must be very busy at that time of year. But the conference is only an hour from your university. I'd be happy to send more details. Please let me know by the end of the week.

OK, everyone, this morning I'm going to show you how to use our new point-of-sale system. It'll go live in all stores on Monday. As you'll see, it's much faster than the old one. To begin, log in with your employee number, which is printed on your ID badge. Then scan the item, and the price will show up automatically. If the customer has a loyalty card, scan that as well. Now, each of you has a practice terminal in front of you. Let's try ringing up a sample order together. You'll also find a quick reference guide next to your terminal, which you can keep.

Want to move ahead in your career? With Bright Path Online, you can learn new skills from home at your own pace. We offer more than two hundred courses in areas such as accounting, project management, and digital marketing. All of them are taught by experts in their fields, and you can watch the lessons on any device. When you've finished, you'll receive a certificate that you can share with your employer. Sign up this month and get your first course for just nineteen dollars. Visit Bright Path Online today.

Hi, everyone. Thanks for helping out with the summer concert series. I just heard from the jazz group that's scheduled for the last concert. They've had to cancel because of a tour in Europe. The Rosa Trio has agreed to perform that evening as well, so we'll still have music. But we'll have to change the posters. Hannah, could you ask the printer to fix that date? And we'll need more chairs this year. Last week, about fifty people had to stand. I'm going to rent a hundred extra chairs from the party store on Main Street.

ARLINGTON — When the Hensons' farm stand lost most of its customers to a new highway bypass in 2022, the family had to act fast. Instead of closing, Nora Henson built a simple Web site where people could order fruit and vegetables for home delivery.

Four years later, the site serves more than 3,000 households. It has also grown to include products from 35 other small farms in the county, all of which pay the Hensons a small commission.

Maple Valley Rail Trail Opens

MAPLE VALLEY (Aug. 2) — The first section of the Maple Valley Rail Trail opened to walkers and cyclists on Saturday. Built along an old railway line, the 12-kilometer section runs from Brookfield to Ashby. A second section, from Ashby to Dunmore, will open next year.

The trail was built by the county with the help of hundreds of volunteers. A nonprofit group, Friends of the Trail, now organizes guided rides and maintains the path. The group is looking for more people to join its weekend work crews.
